---
title: "Arrow"
---

Arrow aesthetics control the shape and size of arrows at the terminal vertices of lines, and apply to layers that draw lines: [line](../../layer/type/line.qmd), [path](../../layer/type/path.qmd) and [segment](../../layer/type/segment.qmd).
These can be useful if lines represent relations and can be mapped if different types of relations need to be reflected.

There are separate aesthetics for arrows at the start and end of lines.
The `arrow` aesthetic is an alias to control `arrowstart` and `arrowend` shapes simultaneously.
The `arrowsize` aesthethic is ditto an alias to control `arrowstartsize` and `arrowendsize` sizes together.
The start and ends of lines are declared directly in segment layers, whereas line and path layers count the first and last observation in a group.

## Literal values
Arrow shapes are specified using named patterns.

| Name | Pattern | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `open` | ![](examples/arrow_open.svg) | V-shape: two strokes converging on the tip |
| `closed` | ![](examples/arrow_closed.svg) | Fatter filled isosceles triangle |
| `stealth` | ![](examples/arrow_stealth.svg) | Dart/chevron as filled concave quadrilateral, thinner in the style of TikZ graphics |
| `latex` | ![](examples/arrow_latex.svg) | Dart/chevron as filled concave quadrilateral, fatter in the style of LaTeX |
| `thin` | ![](examples/arrow_thin.svg) | Thinner filled isosceles triangle |
| `wedge` | ![](examples/arrow_wedge.svg) | Asymmetric triangle |
| `fishtail` | ![](examples/arrow_fishtail.svg) | Inverted V-shape: two strokes diverging as tail |
| `fork` | ![](examples/arrow_fork.svg) | Wider inverted V-shape as tail |
| `feather` | ![](examples/arrow_feather.svg) | Stylised arrow fletching |
| `bar` | ![](examples/arrow_bar.svg) | Orthogonal line at tip |
| `bracket` | ![](examples/arrow_bracket.svg) | Bar with two right-angle protrusions at its ends |
| `cross` | ![](examples/arrow_cross.svg) | Square (Greek) cross angled at 45&deg; from the line |
| `dot` | ![](examples/arrow_dot.svg) | Filled circle |
| `square` | ![](examples/arrow_square.svg) | Filled square |
| `diamond` | ![](examples/arrow_diamond.svg) | Filled diamond |

You can use these names directly when setting the arrow of a line.
Note that the `arrow` setting is an aesthetic alias to set both the `arrowstart` and `arrowend` aesthetics.
You can separate the arrow shapes by using the more specific aesthetics.

```ggsql
DRAW segment
  SETTING arrowstart => 'open', arrowend => 'closed'
```

The `arrowsize` and `arrowstartsize`/`arrowendsize` aesthetics are given in bare numbers.
While individual shapes might deviate, the sizes are roughly in points.
Note that the `arrowsize` aesthetics are irrelevant when `arrow` has not been declared.
The following code sets the size of arrows to 20pt.

```ggsql
DRAW segment
  SETTING arrow => 'open', arrowsize => 20
```

## Palettes

```{ggsql}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Create example data"
CREATE TEMP TABLE edges AS
SELECT * FROM (VALUES
    (0, 0, 1, 1, 'Bottom'),
    (1, 1, 2, 1, 'Bottom'),
    (2, 1, 3, 0, 'Bottom'),
    (0, 3, 1, 2, 'Top'),
    (1, 2, 2, 2, 'Top'),
    (2, 2, 3, 3, 'Top'),
    (1, 1, 1, 2, 'Cross'),
    (2, 2, 2, 1, 'Cross')
) t(x, y, xend, yend, type);
```

The default palette for arrows picks the 15 arrows listed above.

```{ggsql}
VISUALISE x, y, xend, yend FROM edges
DRAW segment 
  MAPPING type AS arrowend
  SETTING arrowsize => 10
```

You can change the arrows by providing a manual palette with shape names as the `TO` clause in scales.

```{ggsql}
VISUALISE x, y, xend, yend FROM edges
DRAW segment 
  MAPPING type AS arrowstart
  SETTING arrowsize => 10
SCALE arrow TO ['latex', 'cross', 'open']
```

You can use different arrows for the start and end by using the specific `arrowstart` and `arrowend` scales for the aesthetics.

```{ggsql}
VISUALISE x, y, xend, yend FROM edges
DRAW segment 
  MAPPING type AS arrow
  SETTING arrowsize => 10
SCALE arrowstart TO ['latex', 'cross', 'open']
SCALE arrowend TO ['wedge', 'dot', 'feather']
```

The `arrowsize` aesthetic takes numeric values and re-scales these to match the `TO` clause.

```{ggsql}
VISUALISE x, y, xend, yend FROM edges
DRAW segment 
  MAPPING x AS arrowsize
  SETTING arrow => 'closed'
SCALE arrowsize TO (5, 20)
```
